CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-CRD01.title: MultiCADSessionEngine — coordinates simultaneous sessions across multiple CADs with shared intent state

pass1.buildNote: Concurrent CAD sessions must share intent state through a lock-guarded store — never two writers racing the same session record.

pass2.systemImpact: MultiCADSessionEngine is the shared-state floor for every cross-CAD unit in CAD-COMPLETE-MS0 — CrossCADIntentFusionEngine (U-CADC-CRD02) and CrossCADConsistencyValidatorEngine (U-CADC-CRD03) both read its session registry, and CADAccessControlRBACABACEngine (U-FS-12) writes session records into it. If the lock-guarded read-modify-write regresses to a last-writer-wins clobber, two CAD bridges silently desync their intent state and downstream consistency validation passes against corrupt input.
csDepth: The session registry is a concurrent map keyed by sessionId — lock granularity matters: a single global lock serializes all CAD sessions (throughput collapse under the 6-bridge fleet), per-session locks risk deadlock if intent fusion needs to read two sessions atomically; prefer per-session locks with a strict lock-ordering rule (sort sessionIds before multi-acquire).

Stale-session reaping is an ABA hazard — a sessionId reused after a crashed session can be mistaken for the live one; tag each session record with a monotonic epoch/nonce so a reader detects the reuse rather than acting on a recycled record.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-CRD02.title: CrossCADIntentFusionEngine — fuses intents from heterogeneous sources (sketch, voice, drawing parse, prior session)

pass1.buildNote: Fuse heterogeneous intent sources by confidence-weighted aggregation — surface disagreement, never silently average conflicting intents.

pass2.systemImpact: CrossCADIntentFusionEngine sits between the heterogeneous intake bridges (sketch/voice/drawing-parse) and the CAD generation pipeline — its fused intent is the input contract for every CAD-COMPLETE-MS0 generation unit. If fusion silently averages conflicting intents instead of surfacing the conflict (per R7), the generation pipeline produces a part that satisfies neither source, and CrossCADConsistencyValidatorEngine cannot catch it because both CADs were fed the same wrong intent.
csDepth: Confidence-weighted aggregation needs calibrated source confidences — an uncalibrated voice-parser that always reports 0.9 will dominate a well-calibrated sketch parser; the fusion must normalize or learn per-source reliability priors, not trust raw self-reported confidence.

Embedding-space similarity for intent matching is O(n·d) per query and sensitive to embedding-model version drift — pin the embedding model version in the persisted intent record so a re-embedded prior session is comparable, otherwise cross-session fusion silently degrades.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-CRD03.title: CrossCADConsistencyValidatorEngine — validates identical semantic output across 2+ CADs within tolerance

pass1.buildNote: Validate semantic equivalence with explicit numeric tolerance — assert identical output across CADs against real reference values, not stubs.

pass2.systemImpact: CrossCADConsistencyValidatorEngine is the correctness gate for the multi-CAD generation pipeline — it consumes outputs of U-CADC-CRD01/CRD02 and any CAD bridge, and CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0's coverage/exit gates (U-CUC15/U-CUC18) depend on it certifying cross-bridge parity. A too-loose epsilon tolerance passes genuinely divergent geometry; a too-tight one floods the regression dashboard with false positives and erodes trust in the whole CAD regression infra.
csDepth: Epsilon-tolerance float comparison must be relative-plus-absolute (a fixed absolute epsilon fails on both micron features and meter-scale assemblies) — use scaled tolerance keyed to the part's bounding box, and define it once as a named constant, not inlined per call site.

Geometric hash comparison is order-sensitive — face/edge enumeration order differs across CAD kernels; the hash must canonicalize (sort by a rotation-invariant key) before hashing or identical geometry from two CADs hashes differently and the validator false-fails.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-LP01.title: CADExecutionOutcomeBusEngine — pub/sub bus for CAD execution results (success/error/timing/collision/regeneration)

csKnowledge: event-driven architecture with typed event payloads (success/error/timing/collision)
pass1.buildNote: Bus must fail-loud on dropped/un-consumed events — silent event loss breaks the closed-loop NN training signal downstream.

pass2.systemImpact: The outcome bus is the single ingest point for the entire CAD closed-loop learning system — U-CADC-LP02 (feedback collector), U-CADC-LP03 (replay buffer), and U-CADC-LP04 (backprop propagator) all subscribe to it. If the bus drops or mis-orders events, every per-CAD NN head (U-CADC-NN02..06) trains on a corrupted reward signal, silently degrading toolpath/feature predictions across all four vendor adapters.
csDepth: A pub/sub bus needs an explicit back-pressure / delivery-guarantee policy: if a slow subscriber (the replay buffer doing disk I/O) blocks the bus, fast subscribers stall — choose bounded-queue + drop-oldest vs unbounded buffer deliberately, and document the at-least-once vs at-most-once semantics.

Event ordering is load-bearing for RL credit assignment: outcome events must carry a monotonic sequence number, since concurrent CAD executions across adapters make wall-clock timestamps insufficient for reconstructing transition order in the replay buffer.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-LP02.title: CADPerAdapterFeedbackCollectorEngine — collects per-adapter metrics and routes to corresponding NN head

csKnowledge: per-key metric aggregation (group-by adapter, running counters)
pass1.buildNote: Route metrics to the CORRECT per-CAD NN head — a mis-routed feedback signal trains the wrong policy; assert routing with real adapter ids in tests.

pass2.systemImpact: Sits between the outcome bus (U-CADC-LP01) and the per-CAD NN heads (U-CADC-NN02..06) — it is the routing layer that decides which head's training signal each metric belongs to. A mis-routed feedback signal trains the wrong vendor policy (e.g. Mastercam outcomes updating the Inventor GNN), a silent correctness failure that only surfaces as degraded prediction quality after U-CADC-LP04 has already back-propagated the bad gradient.
csDepth: Online streaming statistics (running mean/variance) must use a numerically stable algorithm (Welford's) — naive sum-of-squares accumulation loses precision or overflows over a long-running training session with millions of CAD execution events.
The adapter-id to NN-head routing table is a closed enum: an unknown adapter id must fail loud (R12), never default-route to a head — a silent default would poison whichever head is the fallback.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-LP03.title: CADHeadReplayBufferEngine — prioritized replay buffer for closed-loop NN training

csKnowledge: prioritized experience replay (sum-tree / proportional sampling by TD-error priority)
ring buffer with bounded capacity and eviction
pass1.buildNote: Priority sampling must be reproducible — seed the RNG; test that high-priority transitions are sampled more often with real priority values.

pass2.systemImpact: The replay buffer is the training-data store for the closed-loop NN heads — U-CADC-LP04's backprop propagator samples batches from it. If priority sampling is biased or the ring buffer evicts the wrong transitions, the NN heads overfit to a stale slice of CAD execution history and the master brain's policy diverges. Its sampling reproducibility also gates regression-testability of the whole LP01-LP04 loop.
csDepth: Prioritized experience replay with a sum-tree is O(log n) per insert/sample, but a priority update on a full buffer must atomically evict-and-reinsert — an interleaved eviction during sampling can return a transition that no longer exists; guard with a version stamp or copy-on-sample.

Importance-sampling weight correction (beta annealing) is required to debias the non-uniform priority sampling — omitting it introduces a systematic gradient bias that the U-CADC-LP04 propagator cannot detect, since the bias looks like a legitimate loss signal.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-LP04.title: MasterBrainBackpropPropagatorEngine — back-propagates CAD execution outcome to both master policy and per-CAD NN heads

csKnowledge: gradient routing across a two-level policy hierarchy (master + per-CAD heads)
pass1.buildNote: Propagate the SAME outcome gradient to both master policy and the per-CAD head — verify both receive updates; assert with real loss-delta values, divergence guard on NaN/Inf.

pass2.systemImpact: This is the terminal stage of the CAD closed-loop learning system — it converts CAD execution outcomes into weight updates for both the master policy and every per-CAD NN head (the U-CADC-NN01 foundation encoder plus NN02..06 heads). A regression here (wrong gradient routing, missing divergence guard) is the highest-blast-radius failure in the LP chain: it can NaN-poison all six NN engines at once, forcing a full retrain from a checkpoint.
csDepth: Two-level gradient routing (master plus per-CAD head) is a hierarchical-RL credit-assignment problem — the same outcome must flow to the head that acted AND the master that selected it; double-counting or dropping one path produces a subtly wrong policy gradient that still passes shape and finiteness checks.

Gradient clipping and NaN/Inf divergence guards must run BEFORE the optimizer step, not after — an unguarded Inf gradient applied even once permanently corrupts the weight matrix; the guard must fail loud (R12) and skip the batch, never silently zero the gradient.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-NN01.title: CADFoundationEncoderEngine — shared BRep + sketch tokenizer for all per-CAD NN heads

csKnowledge: B-rep + sketch tokenization (geometry -> discrete token sequence)
shared embedding / foundation encoder (frozen backbone feeding multiple heads)
byte-pair / vocabulary construction for geometry primitives
pass1.buildNote: Encoder output schema is a hard contract for all 5 NN heads — version it; a token-vocab change forces every head to retrain. Schema-read before extending.

pass2.systemImpact: The foundation encoder is the shared backbone for all five per-CAD NN heads (U-CADC-NN02..06) — its tokenizer output schema is a hard cross-engine contract. Any change to the B-rep/sketch token vocabulary invalidates every head's learned weights and forces a fleet-wide retrain; U-CADC-LP04's backprop propagator and U-CADC-LP03's replay buffer also assume a stable encoder dimensionality. It is the highest-coupling node in the CAD-NN subsystem.
csDepth: Geometry tokenization must be canonical and order-invariant: the same B-rep solid produced by two different feature histories must tokenize identically, or the heads learn spurious history-dependent features — this requires a deterministic topology traversal sorted by geometric hash, not insertion order.

A frozen-backbone foundation encoder feeding multiple heads needs an explicit version field in its output; consumers must schema-read-check it at load time and refuse a mismatched checkpoint rather than silently producing garbage embeddings.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-NN02.title: MastercamIntentNN — Mastercam-specific policy head (NetHook3 op sequencing + toolpath-strategy prediction)

pass1.buildNote: Consume the U-CADC-NN01 foundation encoder output — do not re-tokenize; assert op-sequence predictions against real Mastercam program data.

pass2.systemImpact: The Mastercam policy head consumes the U-CADC-NN01 foundation encoder and produces op-sequencing plus toolpath-strategy predictions that feed Mastercam automation via the u-bridge-wire-mastercam path. A regression degrades automated Mastercam program generation; because it shares the foundation encoder with NN03..06, an encoder-contract assumption baked here wrong also signals a problem for the sibling heads.
csDepth: Sequence-to-sequence op-order prediction needs a stopping criterion and a max-length cap — an unbounded autoregressive decode can loop emitting operations indefinitely on an out-of-distribution input; cap length and fail loud rather than truncate silently.

Softmax over toolpath-strategy classes yields a probability distribution, not a decision — the consumer needs a calibrated confidence threshold below which it defers to a deterministic strategy, otherwise a low-confidence guess is treated as authoritative.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-NN03.title: HyperCADSIntentNN — hyperCAD-S FT-aware head (Feature Technology recognition + macro selection)

csKnowledge: Feature Technology (FT) recognition over B-rep adjacency graph
pass1.buildNote: hyperCAD-S FT recognition is the input signal — verify against real hyperCAD-S Python-API feature data, not synthetic geometry.

pass2.systemImpact: The hyperCAD-S head turns Feature Technology recognition into macro-selection predictions driving hyperCAD-S Python-API automation. It shares the U-CADC-NN01 foundation encoder with the other four heads; a mis-modeled FT recognition signal here produces wrong macro selections that propagate into hyperCAD-S / hyperMILL CAM downstream.
csDepth: Multi-label classification (a feature set, not a single class) requires per-label thresholds and a label-correlation-aware loss — treating it as multi-class softmax forces mutually-exclusive predictions and silently drops co-occurring features.

FT recognition over a B-rep adjacency graph is sensitive to graph isomorphism: two geometrically-identical features with different face-numbering must yield the same recognition — canonicalize the adjacency graph before encoding.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-NN04.title: Fusion360DiffusionHead — diffusion-based sketch+feature generator targeting adsk.fusion

csKnowledge: denoising diffusion probabilistic model (forward noising + reverse denoising)
pass1.buildNote: Targets adsk.fusion API — generated sketch/feature output must validate against the Fusion 360 object model; test the denoising loop converges with a real seed.

pass2.systemImpact: The Fusion 360 diffusion head generates sketch+feature geometry targeting the adsk.fusion API — it is the generative front-end for Fusion automation. Generated output must validate against the Fusion object model before it reaches the adapter; an unvalidated diffusion sample produces an invalid sketch that crashes the Fusion COM bridge or silently produces wrong geometry downstream in CAM.
csDepth: A DDPM/DDIM reverse-sampling loop is iterative and unbounded in cost — the step schedule (number of denoising steps) is a latency/quality tradeoff that must be a parameter, and the loop needs a convergence/early-exit check plus a hard step cap to avoid runaway sampling.

Diffusion output is continuous-valued; mapping it to the discrete adsk.fusion object model (sketch entities, feature parameters) requires a validated quantization/snapping step — an unconstrained sample produces non-snappable coordinates the Fusion API rejects.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-NN05.title: InventorGNNHead — graph neural network over assembly/mate graph targeting Inventor COM/iLogic

csKnowledge: graph neural network message passing over assembly/mate graph
node + edge feature encoding for parts and mates
pass1.buildNote: The assembly/mate graph is the input — reuse the nn-graph-ms0 GraphSAGE patterns; assert message-passing on a real Inventor assembly with known mate topology.

pass2.systemImpact: The Inventor GNN head does message passing over the assembly/mate graph to produce policy predictions for Inventor COM/iLogic automation. It reuses the nn-graph-ms0 GraphSAGE neighborhood-aggregation patterns; a regression in message passing degrades automated Inventor assembly generation, and a mis-modeled mate-graph signal corrupts assembly constraint inference downstream.
csDepth: GraphSAGE neighborhood aggregation over an assembly graph must handle highly-variable node degree — a base part mated to dozens of components vs a leaf fastener; unnormalized aggregation lets high-degree hub nodes dominate, so use mean/pooling aggregation or degree normalization.

The assembly/mate graph can contain cycles (closed kinematic loops) — message passing must be cycle-safe with a fixed hop count and the graph build must reject self-loops; the nn-graph-ms0 stratified-negative-sampling lesson applies (uniform negatives anti-correlate under heterophily).

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-NN06.title: SolidWorksTransformerHead + FreeCADPolicyRLHead — transformer for SW ISldWorks op sequences; PPO-style RL policy for FreeCAD Python

csKnowledge: transformer self-attention for op-sequence modeling (SolidWorks ISldWorks)
PPO (proximal policy optimization) clipped-surrogate RL objective
advantage estimation (GAE) for the FreeCAD Python policy
pass1.buildNote: Two distinct heads in one unit — keep the SW transformer and FreeCAD PPO policy as separate classes; test the PPO clip ratio and the transformer op-sequence against real data independently.

pass2.systemImpact: This unit ships TWO distinct heads — a transformer for SolidWorks ISldWorks op sequences and a PPO-style RL policy for FreeCAD Python — completing the five-vendor per-CAD NN head set (NN02 Mastercam, NN03 hyperCAD-S, NN04 Fusion, NN05 Inventor, NN06 SW+FreeCAD). Both consume the U-CADC-NN01 foundation encoder and feed U-CADC-LP04's backprop propagator; a regression in either degrades automated SolidWorks/FreeCAD program generation for those two adapters.
csDepth: Bundling two heads in one unit is a coupling hazard — keep the SW transformer and the FreeCAD PPO policy as separate classes with separate test suites and separate dispatcher wiring, or a change to one silently breaks the other (per-file scrutiny should flag any shared mutable state).

PPO's clipped-surrogate objective requires the clip ratio epsilon and the GAE advantage-estimation lambda/gamma to be tuned and tested as real values — a wrong clip ratio either kills learning (too tight) or allows destructive policy jumps (too loose); the transformer head needs the same bounded-decode/max-length guard as NN02.
